text:
emma: quick follow-up from today's all-hands re: GPU supply, region rollouts, and autoscale behavior. dropping a short thread for questions and next steps.
raj: thanks! APAC customers are asking for T4 availability estimates — any firm dates?
emma: APAC burst pools (T4) targeted mid-July for pilot regions. Dedicated (reserved) capacity aiming late Q3. exact zones and capacity numbers next week.
lisa: can you explain the order autoscaler chooses different pools? we need to plan for latency-critical endpoints.
emma: sure — decision order we're using: reserved -> prewarm -> burst (spot/partner) -> model fallbacks. we try to keep p95 latency stable by preferring warm/reserved first.
david: when burst uses spot, what's the eviction strategy? do we transparently route or degrade?
emma: eviction plan: immediate reroute to prewarm/reserved if available; otherwise auto-fallback to quantized or smaller model variant. we won't drop traffic unless ALL paths exhausted.
marcos: ops needs concrete prewarm numbers for cloud orders. what sizes are we recommending per-region?
emma: initial defaults: production-critical routes -> 200 concurrent prewarm slots per major region. APAC pilot: start 50 slots and scale based on 48h telemetry.
jen: can you share an example autoscaler policy we can give product teams (TTLs, warm thresholds)?
emma: pasted sample YAML for teams to copy/tweak:
emma: ```yaml
autoscaler:
  min_replicas: 2
  prewarm_pool: 50
  burst_threshold_qps: 100
  scale_up_cooldown_s: 30
  scale_down_cooldown_s: 300
  fallback_policy:
    - reserved_capacity
    - prewarm_pool
    - burst_spot
    - fallback_model: q1.3b-quantized
```
raj: billing question — for Hosted customers is prewarm charged differently than normal compute?
emma: yes — Dedicated customers get prewarm included in their commit. Hosted PAYG customers see prewarm as short-lived reserved units; we'll add an opt-out flag for teams that don't want prewarm billed.
lisa: how will routing behave when a region is constrained? we need EU-first behavior for some customers.
emma: routing uses region weights + customer tier. enterprise SLA routes get regional priority; PLG traffic can overflow cross-region if allowed by customer routing policy.
marcos: can infra publish a simple GPU-pressure runbook and who to page? we need an on-call map.
emma: action: infra to publish "GPU pressure playbook" by Friday. owner: marcos. will include alert thresholds, on-call matrix, and mitigation steps.
jen: any change to canary windows for autoscaler/serving changes after last week's instability?
emma: yes — new canary: 30m with light traffic check + 2h scale observation. ops will run synthetic load during rollout.
ops-bot: notes uploaded: all-hands infra deck + recording -> https://redwood.company/all-hands/2026-03-20. :spiral_notepad: (deck v10.3)
emma: one last ask: latency-critical teams DM me route names and expected qps so we can prioritize them for the APAC pilot.
david: will Console show prewarm utilization and burst usage? that would help SRE tuning.
emma: yes — Console dashboard will include prewarm utilization, burst %, and per-route latency. beta in ~2 weeks.
raj: can we have a short follow-up sync for product teams to map routes?
emma: scheduling 30m Tue 10am PT. invite from marcos.
marcos: confirmed, agenda: route list, prewarm sizing, playbook review.
emma: closing: we'll publish playbook, the deck link, the sample autoscaler yaml, and run the sync. thanks all! :thumbsup:
